subject: Privacy incident: proposed notice language, evidence escrow and forensic access
messages:
From: Katie Li <katie.li@acme-payments.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-payments.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial ask: incident notice timing + evidence access

Hi Olga —

Quick one from our security team. We are updating our vendor intake and need to confirm two things in writing before we move forward:

1) Your standard customer notice timeline for confirmed data breaches (what window do you commit to for customer notification once you verify a breach?)
2) Whether you will permit a scoped, read-only evidence escrow (hashes, logs, sample event data) to a mutually approved third-party forensic vendor while we coordinate legal/regulatory notices. If you require an NDA or an addendum, please flag that and any lead times.

Can you share proposed language we can include in our DPA appendix? Also any supporting artifacts (SOC 2, SIG/CAIQ answers) would be helpful so our InfoSec can triage.

Thanks,
Katie Li
Security Program Manager
Acme Payments

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Li <katie.li@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask: incident notice timing + evidence access

Hi Katie —

Appreciate the clear asks. High-level answers first:
- Notification window: our typical commitment in the DPA is "without undue delay and no later than 72 hours after confirmation of a security incident affecting Customer Data, except where constrained by law enforcement or legal obligations." We can discuss a customer-specific 48/72/96-hour SLA but 72 hours is our standard starting point.
- Evidence escrow / third-party read-only access: we are open to scoped access via a mutually approved forensics vendor. We require:
  * a narrow statement of work (SOW) for the vendor,
  * an NDA that covers data handling and retention, and
  * a limited-time access window (we typically propose 30 days for initial triage, extendable by agreement).

Attachments: I am sharing our current SOC2 report and the SIG sheet for your review (attached). Rishi, can you add the draft forensics SOW and the preferred access control notes? Laura, please flag any legal redlines for the notice language.

Best,
Olga
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial ask: incident notice timing + evidence access

Katie / Olga —

A few legal points to keep in mind for the DPA appendix and incident-response clause:

1) "Confirmation" definition: we prefer to define "confirmation" as "the point at which Redwood has corroborated, through internal investigation, that an unauthorized access to Customer Data occurred." This avoids committing to notification based solely on unvalidated alerts.

2) Notice window: 72 hours is reasonable as a default. For customers requiring regulatory timing (e.g., HIPAA has different triggers), we can add an exhibit with specific timelines. Suggest language: "Redwood will provide written notice to Customer without undue delay and, where reasonably practicable, within 72 hours of confirmation of an incident impacting Customer Data; where law enforcement or ongoing criminal investigation restricts disclosure, Redwood will promptly notify Customer when such restrictions are lifted."

3) Forensics vendor: recommended contract language items:
  - Vendor access is strictly read-only and for the sole purpose of incident investigation.
  - Vendor must sign Redwood NDA and Customer NDA (if requested).
  - Logs/sample datasets provided must be redacted to the minimum necessary; production full-data exports are disallowed without Customer's explicit written consent.

4) Evidence escrow — red flag: escrowed copies of production data are risky. We recommend escrow limited to:
  - cryptographic hashes,
  - aggregated logs,
  - time-limited snapshots of redacted sample events,
  - forensic artifacts (memory images, stack traces) only under strict controls.

I'll attach a short clause and a 1-page SOW template you can plug into the DPA appendix.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial ask: incident notice timing + evidence access

Katie —

Operational notes and practical proposal from ops/security:

- Confirmed-incident workflow: detection -> triage -> internal confirmation (logs + correlation) -> customer notice -> forensic engagement (if needed). Internal confirmation typically takes 12-48 hours depending on scope.

- Proposed standard offer to customers wanting escrowed evidence:
  1) Redacted sample event dataset (time-bounded, zero PII where avoidable).
  2) Hash set of affected objects with provenance metadata.
  3) Remote, read-only forensic access to a secure, time-limited snapshot environment (no data export).

- Time windows: propose 72-hour notice after confirmation as default; offer 48-hour SLA for enterprise customers on reserved contracts (requires pre-approved SOP and on-call contact details in the DPA exhibit).

- Vendor onboarding: we will accept mutually-approved vendors listed by Customer or vetted ones from our approved vendor list. Vendor must complete our brief technical onboarding (1 business day) and sign NDAs. For urgent matters, we can fast-track to same-day access for pre-approved vendors.

I attached a short quote for an on-call forensic partner (forensic-engagement-quote.pdf) and the low-level access control checklist.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Infra Security
Redwood Inference

Katie —

Thanks for the questions and for the time. To summarize next steps so your legal/compliance team has something to review quickly:

1) Draft DPA appendix language (notice + forensics access) attached as a single-page clause. Key points: 72-hour notice after confirmation (with an enterprise 48-hour option), limited read-only access to a mutually approved forensics vendor, minimum necessary redaction requirement, and 30-day initial access window.

2) We shared SOC2 and SIG artifacts for your InfoSec review.

3) If Acme wants escrow beyond samples and hashes (e.g., full snapshots), we will only consider that under a separate data-escrow agreement with strict controls; please flag specific needs.

4) I'll coordinate with Rishi to provide a vendor SOW and quick onboarding checklist for your team. If you can confirm the preferred vendor(s) or if you want a recommendation from our approved list, we can schedule a 30-minute sync this week.

Please let me know if we should route the draft through a DocuSign link or share a redline via Google Drive.

Best regards,
Olga
